content.text: DON’T FORGET!!!! I convinced the good folks at Underdog to give me $2,500 to give TO YOU!!!! I’m running a FREE Bracket on Underdog (UD APP ONLY TO PLAY btw). Oh, and if I can get more people into this Bracket than Overzet, they’ll add $1000 to the winner. So tell some people. 1st $12502nd $7503rd $500WINNERJordan Spieth +4000 (3 Places)Brooks Koepka +4500 (3 Places)Nicolai Hojgaard +6600 (3 Places)Ryo Hisatsune +6600 (3 Places)Rasmus Hojgaard +8000 (3 Places)Max Homa +11000 (3 Places)Austin Smotherman +11000 (3 Places)YOLOA.J. Ewart +25000 (10 Places)Brian Campbell +200000 (3 Places)TOP CANADIANA.J. Ewart +1600FIRST ROUND LEADERTaylor Moore +6000Zac Blair +11000Zach Bauchou +11000Davis Riley +11000A.J. Ewart +18000LIV SOUTH AFRICAJose Luis Ballester +4000LPGALydia Ko +2500Rose Zhang +3500Jordan Spieth — The driver has started to falter after two straight years of it becoming the best part of Spieth’s game. That’s OK, though—at least this week. With Copperhead requiring players to use driver less often, Spieth needs to rely on his irons, chipping, and putting, all of which have been spiking over the last six weeks.Brooks Koepka — After +8.17 SG: Ball Striking at Sawgrass, that’s three elite ball-striking performances in four starts for Brooks. Eventually, the putter is going to stabilize… hopefully.Nicolai Hojgaard — King Nicolai is one of the few in the field who is green across the board in 2026 (positive in all four main SG metrics). His numbers are almost identical to Xander’s. Nicolai has made five starts in 2026 and doesn’t have a finish worse than T27.Ryo Hisatsune — Hisatsune very quietly snuck up to T13 at THE PLAYERS, finishing eighth in the field in ball striking. He’s top 10 in the field in total driving, already has three top-10s in 2026, and finished T4 here a year ago. Just needs to warm his putter back up.Rasmus Hojgaard — It’s rough with Rasmus coming off two missed cuts. Sawgrass, whatever, but Puerto Rico isn’t a good look. Still, in his four starts prior, he posted a better finish each time, peaking with a T9 at PGA National to kick off the Florida swing. The approach play has remained consistent and, outside of Sawgrass, he has been one of the best putters on TOUR this season. He also finished T3 at the Sanderson Farms this fall, a course that has seen a lot of crossover through the years.Austin Smotherman — There is a WD watch for Smotherman in effect, as his wife is due to give birth Monday. That said, it’s tough to overlook what he’s been doing this season. No player is gaining more strokes per round on approach than THE SMOTHER MAN, and he’s coming off a week where he led the field in driving at THE PLAYERS. If he can figure out how to make a putt on the weekend, he’s live to win. No official word on whether or not he plans to keep playing if he’s in contention, but I’m good with wagering on a guy with little status, no wins, and who likely needs the million dollars to stick around. In DFS, another story (more below).Max Homa — Obviously, Homa’s not at the level of a few years back, but there are signs of those peaks returning. He’s not driving it out of bounds every three holes… that’s a positive! And now his irons are improving, and he’s gained on the greens in eight of nine starts. The birdies will be there; if he can just curb his addiction to squares on the scorecard, he’s live at his number.A.J. Ewart — Coolbet has boosted Ewart to +1600 as Low Canadian if you’re in Canada (outside Ontario) and want to take advantage. I bet that. As an outright? Likely wishful thinking to actually contend to win, but there are positive signs. Unlike most players in his range, he’s actually won something in the somewhat recent past. Ewart only has his TOUR card because he won Q-School. Plus, he went to college at Barry University just outside Miami and twice played in the Copperhead Classic, finishing 2nd and 7th in his two appearances. So he’s not coming in with no experience on the grounds. Probably more relevant, Ewart has done all his damage with his irons and putting so far this season. We’ve seen enough mid-drivers contend at Copperhead while excelling in those two areas.Brian Campbell — Look, Campbell won twice last year and now he’s 2000/1. I’ll make a donation.Valspar Championship 2026 Final Bets, One & Done | Insights From CopperheadVALSPAR CHAMPIONSHIP DraftKings PicksThe Valspar CHAMPIONSHIP Picks, Bets, One and Done The Valspar CHAMPIONSHIP Research, Sleepers & Course Breakdown2026 March Madness Bracket Picks | 2026 NCAA Tournament Picks, OddsNo wave advantage has materialized this week at Copperhead. That doesn’t mean it won’t, but there’s nothing indicating that at the moment. What we do see is pretty breezy conditions all day long, with both mornings hitting higher gusts than the afternoon. I wouldn’t be shocked if that evened out, since the wind is usually stronger in the afternoon, generally speaking. Keep checking back, especially Friday, as a wave may get slightly better conditions for DK RD2 showdown.WIND TOWER: Tarpon Springs / Rolling OaksWhile I bet Smotherman and will run him through large GPP lineups, I’m keeping him out of any single entries and 3-max. I do think if he’s in the mix, he’ll stay and try to win—hence the bet and large GPP exposure. However, if he’s out of contention, I can see him bolting should the baby come. For me, he’s not likely enough to outperform Bud Cauley, Taylor Moore, Lucas Glover, Mac Meissner, etc. at essentially the same price to inherit the risk where a good 6/6 becomes a lackluster 5/6 on Saturday or Sunday. I have no idea if that’s a good strategy or not, but it’s what I’m doing.On the DK Show, Blickle and I talked through different lineup constructions, and I decided to fade a lot of the top of the board opting to start building at Jacob Bridgeman and down. Not completely, but a lot. Again, what I’m doing likely isn’t optimal. This led to a lot of balanced lineups and some stacked 5/1 stars-and-scrubs rosters. If you want to squeeze in a few studs, I used Michael Kim, David Ford, Michael Brennan, Marty Dou, Zach Bauchou, AJ Ewart, Davis Riley, and Jeremy Paul as my 6K mix-and-match players. Paul is only 6,200 if you reallllllllly need to make something workAt an event where GIR is low vs the PGA average overall, and well under 50% from off the fairway, I’ve decided to go lower on three players who are either struggling with their accuracy, irons, or BOTH!!!! There is a 30% PGA Only boost and a 50% overall boost too.
